newsitem.title: USA: Alternative Resources off on revenue talk - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Alternative Resources off on revenue talk - analysts.

text.p: Alternative Resources Corp shares fell 4-3/8 to 27-1/8 Tuesday amid talk the company will not meet expectations for third quarter revenues, security analysts and traders said.
"There is a perception out there that revenues will fall short...but this is an incredible overreaction," said Mark Marcon, an analyst for Cleary Gull Reiland & McDevitt Inc.
The company was not immediately available for comment and said it has not released a statement.
Earlier Alternative Resources, which provides technical staff for information services companies, hit an intra-day low of 26-1/4. Monday, the stock closed four lower at 31-1/2.

Analysts said, however, the Lincolnshire, Ill.-based company is expected to meet earnings per share expectations. The consensus on Wall Street is $0.22 a share, versus $0.17 in third quarter last year.
"I believe they are going to make the number," said John Larson, an analyst for GS2 Securities Inc.

Cleary Gull's Marcon said he pegged revenues for third quarter at $52.5 million, a number which he said is the low-end of the range of analysts' estimate. Last year Alternative Resources reported third quarter revenues of $40 million.
"They'll be around my number or slightly short," he said.
The potential revenues shortfall, Marcon added, may be the result of switching the focus to bigger, long-term accounts and outsourcing contracts, which he said will likely pay off in the future.
"In focusing on the long term they have let some short-term business possibly go," Marcon said. "I'm a table-pounding buyer at this point."
